sentences.text: GTA 6 needs up to two hundred and twelve gigabytes, and Take-Two reported over thirty-two million copies sold before release.
So how do you ship that without breaking the internet?
Step one: preloads opened over a week early, so the bytes could move before launch day.
Downloads like this come from C D Ns: copies cached on edge servers near players.
Comcast said the first forty-eight hours of preloads were the largest single event in its network history.
The game unlocked at midnight local time, rolling around the planet from New Zealand.
The first patch was about one gigabyte on PS5, not another two hundred.
One thing can't be preloaded: the licence check.
Hours before launch, PlayStation Network struggled, and a downloaded game can still need that check to start.
The lesson: move the bytes early, stagger the spike, and find the one dependency everyone hits at once.
Save it for your next release plan.
